task: The repeat-block breaker keys repeated gate failures on a 200-character prefix of the refusal text, so genuinely different blockers collapse onto one key and freeze a story that is actually making progress.
outcome: Fixing one unmet precondition at a time no longer looks like a stuck loop: each distinct blocker gets its own repeat-block key, while a genuinely identical blocker still accumulates to the trip threshold.
facts: A repeat-block breaker already exists (B-bbaf) in core/convergence-breaker.ts; its contract comment says it counts same-(command,reason) failures.
gateFailureDigest normalizes the reason then slices to 200 chars before hashing.
For ProofStory gate failures the first 200 normalized chars are an invariant banner; the Diagnostic gaps section naming the unmet precondition sits far beyond it.
Digit normalization collapses trigger reasons (4) and (6) to the same text.
Reproduced on B-cc54 itself: three distinct blockers shared one key and tripped gate-repeat 3>=2.
Clearing the resulting freeze requires an interactive human TTY ack, which an unattended run cannot obtain.
The spike resolved the only open unknown: review-convergence.ts keys on a finding-count trend, not refusal identity, and is advisory-only, so it cannot observe this failure mode.
constraints: Must stay fail-closed: a genuinely stuck loop must still reach the trip threshold.
Must not rewrite finding attribution or auto-satisfy any gate.
Must not change behaviour for reasons that carry no structured signal.
The signal vocabulary must be genuinely bounded (F-002): any bracketed lowercase word would let a loop mint a fresh key per attempt and escape the brake.
